a: TDD writes a failing test first, then code, then refactor.
BDD describes behavior in business-readable scenarios.
Smoke is shallow critical path; regression is broader recheck.
Many unit, fewer integration, few e2e tests.
Parallel tests need isolation to avoid shared-state flakes.
Deterministic seed data makes failures reproducible.
Mock clocks when asserting time-based behavior.
Mock external HTTP in unit tests for speed and reliability.
Coverage gaps highlight untested branches, not guaranteed correctness.
Run critical tests before production deploys.
